title: Daily Market Digest: November 02, 2026
subtitle: US Markets Close Mixed as Tech Wobbles, Dow Gains

items.headline: Tech Sector Drags Down Broader Market; Dow Rebounds Amid Oil Price Drop
items.summary: US equities closed Monday with a mixed performance, as an early rally faded due to continued weakness in technology and AI-related stocks. Investors largely rotated out of riskier tech assets into more defensive areas of the market. The Dow Jones Industrial Average managed to post gains, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite ended lower. This shift occurred against a backdrop of falling oil prices and ahead of the critical US midterm elections.

items.headline: S&P 500
items.statContext: The S&P 500 erased morning gains to close down, influenced by the tech sector's decline.

items.headline: NASDAQ Composite
items.statContext: The tech-heavy Nasdaq tumbled, marking a significant drop as investors continued to dump AI-related stocks.

items.headline: Dow Jones Industrial Average
items.statContext: The Dow bucked the broader market trend, advancing as investors shifted into industrial and defensive sectors.

items.headline: IDEXX Laboratories Surges on Strong Earnings
items.summary: Veterinary diagnostics company Idexx Laboratories leaped after reporting stronger-than-expected quarterly profit and revenue, alongside raising its full-year forecasts.

items.headline: United Airlines Gains as Oil Prices Fall
items.summary: United Airlines climbed, buoyed by a significant drop in oil prices and renewed investor optimism following its recent third-quarter earnings report and upbeat forward guidance.

items.headline: Lumentum Tumbles on Acquisition News
items.summary: Lumentum shares fell sharply after Marvell Technology announced an all-stock deal to acquire the optical and photonic products maker, sparking concerns about the transaction.

items.headline: Intel Plummets on Weak Outlook
items.summary: Intel Corporation plummeted after providing a weak forecast for the current quarter, citing a slowdown in PC sales despite surpassing its third-quarter earnings and revenue estimates.

items.headline: Marvell Technology Declines Post-Acquisition Announcement
items.summary: Marvell Technology fell significantly following its announcement to acquire Lumentum, with the broader semiconductor sector experiencing a selloff and investor concerns about the deal.

items.headline: Amazon Shares Dip on Disappointing Earnings
items.summary: Shares of Amazon.com fell after the company reported third-quarter 2026 earnings and revenues that missed analysts' expectations.

items.headline: Federal Reserve Holds Rates Steady at October Meeting
items.summary: The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to maintain the federal funds target range between 3.75% and 4.00% at its October meeting. Separately, Fed Chair Kevin Warsh announced a revised meeting schedule for 2027 and 2028, reducing the number of annual rate-setting votes to focus on strategy.

items.headline: US Manufacturing Activity Remains Healthy in October
items.summary: October saw robust US manufacturing performance, with the S&P Global Manufacturing PMI registering 54.9 and the ISM Manufacturing PMI at 55.5, both comfortably above the 50-point threshold indicating expansion.

items.headline: Oil Prices Tumble Amid Middle East Diplomatic Hopes
items.summary: Brent crude prices fell 7.6% to $104.77 per barrel, and WTI crude dipped below $100, driven by optimism surrounding renewed diplomatic efforts for peace talks between the US and Iran in the Middle East.

items.headline: Tech Sector Continues to Lag, Energy Leads
items.summary: Technology stocks were the worst performers, with the Information Technology Select Sector SPDR ($XLK) declining 4.9%. This was largely due to ongoing concerns about the profitability and sustainability of massive AI infrastructure investments. In contrast, the Energy Select Sector SPDR ($XLE) gained 1.9%, leading gains as investors rotated into traditional energy.

items.headline: Markets Eye US Midterm Elections and Corporate Earnings
items.summary: Investors are closely watching the US midterm elections scheduled for November 3rd, with anticipation of how shifts in congressional power could impact fiscal policy. Meanwhile, major companies like Apple ($AAPL) and Palantir ($PLTR) reported earnings after market close, with their shares sliding in after-hours trading.
